then.text: Still cracked. Off you go and break something else. Legally.
Have another go at a cipher, just for fun?

else.text: Hut 8. Turing's team broke the German navy's Enigma in here. Today I've a practice message for you: a Caesar shift, the oldest cipher there is.

then.text: Lovely. Enigma used the same idea, except the shift changed with every key pressed, and an army machine could be set up in about 159 million million million ways.
That's why it took the Bombe, and thousands of people, and a lot of tea.
